messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - GPU pool 'realtime-gpu-pool' reporting capacity exhaustion and high queue growth. Autoscale alerts firing: HPA not increasing replica count for model-serving pods. Pager routed to #incidents and @oncall-sre.
claire_sre: acknowledging, I'm on it — looking at autoscaler + metrics pipeline.
claire_sre: quick TL;DR from the alert: backend queue length hitting 1200 requests, 95th latency > 8s, pod CPU low but GPU util at ~100% on all nodes. HPA target (custom prometheus metric) hasn't moved for 12m.
alex_platform: seeing the same in the infra dashboards — prom-adapter scrape times spiking. Promise to paste graphs.
maria_runtime: @claire_sre which model group? Is this embeddings or generation?
josh_support: first customer report came in ~10m ago: increased 429s for embeddings endpoint, some requests time out.
claire_sre: affected: realtime embeddings (model: redwood-embed-large) and a few low-latency gen routes pinned to the realtime-gpu-pool.
prometheus-bot: Prometheus target 'prometheus-adapter:443/metrics' last scrape: 00:09:24 ago, 50% scrape failures.
claire_sre: running quick checks:
```
kubectl get hpa -n inference realtime-embed-hpa -o wide
# shows TARGETS: prometheus/custom/realtime_queue_length: 1200/1
kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=realtime-embed -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.cpu,GPU:.status.allocatable.gpu
```
claire_sre: HPA is configured on custom metric `realtime_queue_length` from prometheus-adapter. Adapter timestamps are stale. Adapter logs show `503 upstream timeout` and `failed to translate metric` errors.
alex_platform: pinging the prom-adapter host, network looks OK from infra side, but the prom-adapter process has been GCing and OOM-killing on a few nodes. Last restart at 11:07.
maria_runtime: is there a fallback in the routing layer? can we send non-critical requests to dedicated pool or a lower-capacity model?
claire_sre: yes, we have a routing policy `realtime-fallback` that sends heavy queries to `realtime-gpu-pool-burst` or to `cpu-embed-fallback` (slower). I'm going to flip the policy to route best-effort traffic to fallback to relieve pressure. Executing now.
```
# Traffic switch
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/routing/swap -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings","policy":"realtime-fallback"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx'
```
claire_sre: switched routing for non-SLA customers. Monitoring queue. Queue dropped from 1200 -> 700 over 3m. :white_check_mark: partial relief.
josh_support: updating impacted customers: sending a note to customers flagged as non-SLA. High-tier customers still on original pool — we need capacity for them.
anya_pm: Do we have any customers on SLOs publicly affected? We should draft a status page message.
claire_sre: high-tier customers see degraded latency but not 5xxs yet; a handful of orgs reported 429s before the reroute. I'll coordinate with Josh for status.
alex_platform: mitigation plan — immediate: restart prom-adapter pods on nodes with OOM history, increase prom-adapter replica count to 3, and temporarily enable HPA fallback to use node CPU metrics if prom custom metrics are unavailable. Long term: increase adapter memory, add circuit-breakers for metric queries.
maria_runtime: can we hot scale the GPU nodepool? We have reserved capacity in us-west-2 if we bump the nodepool size +1. That's probably the fastest way to get capacity for SLA traffic.
claire_sre: I'll request an emergency scale from infra. @infra-team can you spin +2 nodes in realtime-gpu-pool (g4dn.12x) now?
alex_platform: infra confirmed — starting nodepool scale up, ETA ~6m to join cluster.
prometheus-bot: prom-adapter endpoint recoveries: successful scrape rate improved to 70% after restart.
claire_sre: while nodes spin up, I'm going to force HPA to ignore stale custom metrics and scale by override to 10 replicas for realtime embedding service.
```
kubectl scale deployment/realtime-embed --replicas=10 -n inference
kubectl annotate hpa/realtime-embed-hpa redwood/override-scaling="true" -n inference
```
claire_sre: replicas now 10. Queue trending down to 220 in last 6m. Latency 95th back to ~2.2s for SLA customers.
ben_oncall: joining handoff — any outstanding tasks I should own?
claire_sre: handing off after infra nodes join and prom-adapter replica count holds. Tasks for you: monitor prom-adapter scrapes, verify HPA reads custom metric again (no override), coordinate a safe rollback of routing policy after stabilizes, and run postmortem checklist.
ben_oncall: ack. I'll keep the channel and start a postmortem doc.
anya_pm: customer impact summary for status: "Partial degradation for embedding endpoints from ~11:02–11:24 UTC. Non-SLA traffic rerouted. High-tier customers experienced elevated latency; 429s were reported briefly. No data loss." I'll work with Josh to publish.
josh_support: posted update to status page and customer comms draft in #support-drafts.
alex_platform: prom-adapter memory bumped (requested PR deployed), replicas 3. Adapter logs show earlier stacktrace: `panic: runtime: out of memory` in translation worker. We're also adding rate-limiting on internal scrape queries to avoid GC spikes.
maria_runtime: follow-ups for postmortem: - validate HPA metric fallbacks - add canary for prom-adapter config - test routing failover automation
claire_sre: rough timeline for incident notes: detection 11:02 UTC, pager 11:04, routing reroute 11:12, manual scale 11:18, nodes joined 11:24, stabilization 11:30.
ben_oncall: recording those. I'll own the action to add a temporary alarm to detect adapter OOMs earlier.
anya_pm: open question: do we want to expand reserved burst capacity for realtime-gpu-pool? I'll create a proposal ticket.
claire_sre: also filing a bug: HPA should fallback to CPU-based policy if last successful prom-adapter scrape older than 60s.
prometheus-bot: alert cleared: HPA alert for realtime-embed-hpa (firing -> resolved).
claire_sre: final check — queue steady ~80, no new 429s reported in last 10m. I’m going to hand off to @ben_oncall for overnight monitoring and postmortem. Escalation: none required to exec.
ben_oncall: ack, taking over. I'll post the postmortem draft in ~2h. Leaving channel open.
josh_support: closing loop with customers; will attach incident summary.
anya_pm: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: ben (lead), alex (infra), maria (runtime), claire (incident timeline).
claire_sre: incident resolved for now. Great work. :tada:
